sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Strategic Pivot**: Humayun's obsession with the **Gaur (Bengal)** campaign allowed Sher Khan to consolidate power in Bihar and the Gangetic plains.
• **The Chunar Siege**: Humayun spent months besieging the **Chunar Fort** (1537-38), which was the 'Gateway to the East', giving Sher Khan time to secure his rear.
• **The Bengal Trap**: Humayun renamed Gaur as **Jannatabad** (Abode of Paradise) and indulged in luxury, losing touch with the political developments in Delhi and Agra.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: The **Battle of Chausa (1539)** and **Battle of Kannauj/Bilgram (1540)** represent the decisive military failures that ended Humayun's first reign.

items.definition: The name given by Humayun to the city of Gaur in Bengal, symbolizing his detachment from administrative reality.
The river where Humayun was saved from drowning by a water-carrier (Nizam) after the Battle of Chausa; later rewarded with a day's kingship.

items.title: Major Strategic Failures
items.content:
• **Intelligence Failure**: Humayun underestimated the Afghan resurgence led by Sher Khan.
• **Logistical Overstretch**: Maintaining a long supply line from Delhi to Bengal proved fatal.

items.title: Consequences of the Struggle
items.content:
• **Political**: Temporary end of Mughal rule in India (1540-1555).
• **Administrative**: Introduction of Sher Shah's reforms (Land revenue, currency, and communication).

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'C-B-K' (Chunar, Bengal, Kannauj).
• **Decoded Meaning**: Chunar (1537) -> Bengal Campaign (1538) -> Kannauj (1540).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses the Battle of Chausa and Kannauj. Remember: Chausa was a surprise ambush; Kannauj was a full-scale pitched battle where weather played a role.
Mains Value Addition: Use the phrase 'Strategic indecisiveness of Humayun vs. Calculated opportunism of Sher Khan' to analyze the power shift.

keyTakeaways: Humayun's Bengal campaign was a strategic blunder that isolated him from his power base.
Sher Khan utilized the 'Guerrilla' and 'Surprise' tactics effectively against the Mughal heavy cavalry.
The defeat at Kannauj forced Humayun into a 15-year exile, leading to the Sur Interregnum.
